mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate relative to its recent 12-month average compresses equity valuations through increased discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above its 12-month moving average (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return >0).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.0% signals a tight labor market that typically precedes accelerated inflation and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return >0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL (above 5.0% annualized) and FEDFUNDS (above 3.5%) signal a high-inflation, high-rate regime that triggers equity sell-offs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 5.0 and FEDFUNDS > 3.5 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return >0).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions (defined by strong GDP growth and robust consumer spending), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to profit-taking and rising rate expectations, even though the signal is always-on.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return >0).

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market conditions (as measured by high employment growth) typically support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return <0).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below its 12-month moving average signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as economic growth concerns mount.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when INDPRO < 12-month moving average (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return >0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 5.0%) and declining housing starts (HOUST < 1500.0) signal a weakening economy amid high inflation, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 5.0 and HOUST < 1500.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return >0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days (approximately one quarter).
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when RSAFS > 3-month moving average (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return <0).
